classification.difficultyReason: Construct specified acute and obtuse angles using a common baseline.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Copy the diagram below, leaving about 6 cm of space above the diagram for angles to be drawn.

spec.description: Horizontal baseline beginning at A, passing through P and continuing beyond P; no arrowhead or numerical length.
spec.mathematics: A is the origin of ray AP.

answer.short: A horizontal ray beginning at $A$ and passing through $P$, with about 6 cm clear above it.
answer.worked: Draw a horizontal ray from $A$ through $P$, continuing beyond $P$. Leave about 6 cm above the copied ray for the constructions in part b.

spec.description: Copied baseline; drawing clearance is supplied by the response space.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use your protractor to construct rays, pointing upwards, that make angles with the ray $AP$ of:

answer.worked: Centre the protractor at $A$ with its zero along $AP$. Mark $24^\circ$ above the baseline and draw a ray from $A$ through the mark.
Centre the protractor at $A$ with zero along $AP$. Mark $160^\circ$ counterclockwise, using the obtuse reading, and draw the ray through the mark.
With the protractor centred at $A$ and zero along $AP$, mark $70^\circ$ above the baseline. Draw the ray from $A$ through the mark.
With the protractor centred at $A$ and zero along $AP$, mark $170^\circ$ counterclockwise. Draw the ray through the mark, just above the leftward horizontal direction.
Centre the protractor at $A$, align zero with $AP$ and mark $82^\circ$ above the baseline. Draw the ray from $A$ through the mark.
Centre the protractor at $A$, align zero with $AP$ and mark $116^\circ$ counterclockwise. Draw the ray through the obtuse-angle mark.
Centre the protractor at $A$, align zero with $AP$ and mark $5^\circ$ above the baseline. Draw the ray through the mark.
Centre the protractor at $A$, align zero with $AP$ and mark $133^\circ$ counterclockwise. Draw the ray through the obtuse-angle mark.

spec.description: Completed common construction; all eight rays originate at A and point above AP.
spec.mathematics: Counterclockwise directions from AP: 24, 160, 70, 170, 82, 116, 5 and 133 degrees.
